correctness.rationale: The actual RESULT.md and verification source were read at the frozen Git tree. Phase covariance turns the constrained two-vector radius into inf_{t≥0}(||tI+T||−qt): Perron singular vectors attain the envelope for q above the norm-plateau overlap, and the norming subspace fills overlaps [0,q0] below it. Comparison of the positive tridiagonal Gram matrix with an intact central principal path and the full unweighted path bounds F_n(t) between square roots of 1+t²+2t cos[π/(n−2K)] and 1+t²+2t cos[π/(n+1)], independent of defect weights. On compact t, n²(F_n−1−t)→−π²t/[2(1+t)]; for c>0 the minimizing t stays compact by 1+t≤2n²(1−cos[π/(n−2K)])/c. Optimizing π²t/[2(1+t)]−ct gives the claimed squared positive part. At c=0 direct ordinary-radius cosine bounds yield π²/2. This covers fixed K, c≥0, n>2K+3, all weights in (0,1] with specified unit bulk, and no assertion for growing K or higher asymptotics. Finite NumPy/SciPy tests of tridiagonal spectra are corroborative, not a limit proof.

originality.rationale: The fixed-n exact Jordan-shift q-radius envelope, unit plateau and quadratic exit have already been established by the published 2026-10-11 Resultary theorem (full original RESULT.md read). The new target is not those ingredients but uniform double scaling n→∞ with q=1−c/n² and arbitrarily varying finitely supported positive endpoint defects. The 2014 weighted-shift article concerns q=1 ordinary radius; 2007 periodic weighted shifts concern infinitely repeating modulations, not independently changing finite endpoint defects. No read prior result implies the coefficient uniform in all endpoint weights.

value.rationale: Uniform leading asymptotics under adversarially vanishing fixed boundary weights show a nontrivial spectral stability phenomenon at the natural n^{-2} q-radius crossover, and pinpoint threshold c=π²/2. This is not a constant substitution into the known fixed-n Jordan formula: it is a uniform theorem for an infinite class of perturbed operators with no lower-bound control at the edge; such robustness is useful when studying finite sections and boundary conditions.
